title: The Effect of Carbetocin on Cardiac Repolarization: A Randomized, Placebo-and Positive-Controlled QT/QTc Study in Healthy Adults

citation.title: The Effect of Carbetocin on Cardiac Repolarization: A Randomized, Placebo-and Positive-Controlled QT/QTc Study in Healthy Adults

what_it_measured.text: This randomized, placebo-and positive-controlled trial evaluated the effect of a single intravenous infusion of a supratherapeutic dose (650 μg) of carbetocin over 45 min on cardiac repolarization in healthy adults (N = 42).

QT interval prolongation of clinical relevance has been reported for oxytocin and, due to the structural similarity between the two compounds, the possibility that carbetocin has a similar effect cannot be ruled out. • What Question Did This Study Address ○ To determine whether carbetocin prolongs the QT interval, and if so, to what extent, the effects of intravenous infusion of a supratherapeutic dose of carbetocin (650 μg) on cardiac repolarization were evaluated by continuously collected electrocardiograms (cardiodynamic ECGs) in healthy adults, with placebo control and active control (moxifloxacin).

dose.text: This randomized, placebo-and positive-controlled trial evaluated the effect of a single intravenous infusion of a supratherapeutic dose (650 μg) of carbetocin over 45 min on cardiac repolarization in healthy adults (N = 42).

In Part B, participants received 3 treatments in a crossover design with randomized sequence: A single infusion of carbetocin (650 μg over 45 min) as determined in Part A; a single IV infusion of matching placebo; and a single IV infusion of matching placebo with a single, open-label oral dose of moxifloxacin hydrochloride, 400 mg (Figure 1).

route.text: In Part B, participants received 3 treatments in a crossover design with randomized sequence: A single infusion of carbetocin (650 μg over 45 min) as determined in Part A; a single IV infusion of matching placebo; and a single IV infusion of matching placebo with a single, open-label oral dose of moxifloxacin hydrochloride, 400 mg (Figure 1).

This dosing regimen was anticipated to result in supratherapeutic carbetocin plasma concentrations based on predictions from a PK model for an unpublished PK study evaluating a 1-min IV infusion of 100 μg carbetocin in healthy women.

Participants and administering staff were blind to the treatment sequence allocation. 2.4 | Interventions In Part A, the effect of a single IV infusion of 650μg carbetocin over 45min on heart rate was evaluated.

endpoint.text: The primary endpoint was placebo-corrected change from baseline in QT interval (ΔΔQTc) using the most appropriate heart rate (HR) correction method.

In Part B, secondary endpoints for carbetocin administration included: Absolute values, change from baseline, and placebocorrected change from baseline in HR, PR, RR, QRS, and QTcF; abnormalities in T-wave morphology and pathologic U-waves; and pharmacokinetic parameters.
2.5 | Endpoints In Part A, the primary endpoint was the observed HR values and change from baseline of HR from 45 min before through 4 h after carbetocin administration.

reported_results.text: The estimated mean placebo-corrected oQTcI change from baseline was 4.5 msec (90% CI: 3.4, 5.6) at the high clinical exposure level of 12.4 ng/mL following a single intravenous infusion of 867 μg/h carbetocin.
During intravenous infusion of carbetocin, the mean HR change from baseline reached a maximum of 16.7 bpm.
The estimated mean ΔΔoQTcI (90% CI) was 4.5 msec (3.4, 5.5) at the high clinical exposure level of 12.4 ng/mL.

Using the model-predicted, placebo-corrected change from baseline in oQTcI, following a single IV infusion of 650 μg carbetocin over 45 m, the estimated mean ΔΔoQTcI (90% CI) was 4.5 (3.4, 5.6) msec at the high clinical exposure level of 12.4 ng/mL (Figure 6b).
Data are shown as estimated mean (90% confidence interval).

Shaded area shows the 95% confidence interval. (bottom) Estimated placebo-corrected, optimized, individualized heart rate–corrected QT interval (ΔΔoQTcI) versus timematched plasma carbetocin concentration.
